title: Medical Office Replacement Property Sourcing
name: Medical Office Replacement Property Sourcing
metaTitle: Medical Office Replacement Property Sourcing in Los Angeles, CA
metaDescription: Sourcing medical office replacement property in Los Angeles for a 1031 exchange, matched to lease term, parking ratio, and seismic retrofit status before day 45.

sections.html: Selling a medical office building in Los Angeles and rolling the proceeds into a 1031 exchange puts a hard clock on finding a replacement that clears underwriting on more than a comparable cap rate alone. Medical office trades on a narrower set of numbers than general office — parking ratio, tenant improvement payback, and seismic retrofit status move a building in or out of range fast, and the identification list needs to reflect that from the first week.

sections.heading: Medical Office Stock From the Westside to the San Fernando Valley
sections.html:
Los Angeles medical office buildings run from 6,000-square-foot single-suite properties to 45,000-square-foot multi-tenant blocks, and pricing splits along that line. Stabilized multi-tenant medical office has generally traded in the 5.5% to 6.75% cap rate range, while single-tenant, investment-grade credit deals price tighter, closer to 5.0% to 5.75%, reflecting the longer weighted-average lease term and lower rollover risk.

Submarket location tracks hospital and health-system anchors: Beverly Grove and Miracle Mile properties draw demand tied to Cedars-Sinai, Westwood and Century City buildings sit near UCLA Health, Encino and Sherman Oaks stock benefits from Providence Saint Joseph, and South Bay medical office trades on proximity to Torrance Memorial and Harbor-UCLA. Physician-group leases in Los Angeles typically run seven to ten years with 3% annual escalations, which sets the baseline for underwriting rent growth on the replacement side.

sections.heading: Line Items That Move a Medical Office Deal In or Out of Range
sections.html:
Before a medical office property goes on the identification list, run it against the checklist that actually changes basis and cash flow:

  • Remaining lease term measured against the exchanger's intended hold period
  • Tenant improvement allowance already amortized into rent versus still owed to the tenant
  • Expense reimbursement structure — full-service gross, modified gross, or true NNN
  • Parking ratio, with 4 to 6 stalls per 1,000 square feet as the practical floor for imaging and multi-specialty tenants
  • Seismic retrofit status for soft-story wood-frame or non-ductile concrete construction, and who bears the retrofit cost
  • Title 24 and ADA compliance exposure at the individual suite level

sections.heading: Sizing the Identification List Against the 45-Day Clock
sections.html:
When the replacement basis runs smaller than the relinquished medical office, the debt-and-equity math has to close the gap without triggering boot — either the replacement carries equal or greater debt than what was paid off, or the exchanger adds cash to match. That math should run on every candidate before it makes the list, not after.

Multi-tenant medical office with several physician-group leases takes longer to underwrite because each tenant needs an estoppel certificate before closing, and estoppel turnaround from small practice groups tends to run slower than from a national credit tenant. Single-tenant, investment-grade medical office closes faster but trades at a tighter cap rate, so the identification list should mix both profiles rather than betting the window on one.

sections.heading: Financing a Medical Office Replacement in the Current Rate Environment
sections.html:
Lenders active in Los Angeles medical office have generally underwritten stabilized, multi-tenant buildings to 60% to 65% loan-to-value with a minimum debt-service-coverage ratio around 1.25x, tightening further for buildings with a single physician-group tenant whose lease runs fewer than seven years. Buildings carrying deferred seismic retrofit work typically see that loan-to-value ceiling pulled down further until the retrofit scope and cost are documented.

Matching the achievable loan amount on a medical office candidate to the debt paid off on the relinquished property is the same exercise that applies across every asset class on the identification list, and it should be run before a property is chosen rather than discovered during loan underwriting weeks before the 180-day deadline.

sections.heading: Coordinating Financial Review Before the List Closes
sections.html: Rent roll and trailing-12 review on each medical office candidate should happen in parallel with identification, not after a property is chosen, since estoppel language and reimbursement reconciliation can shift the effective yield by a full percentage point. That financial review feeds directly into what the qualified intermediary needs on file and what a tax advisor will want to see before Form 8824 gets prepared.

faqs.q: What cap rate range should I expect on Los Angeles medical office replacement property?
faqs.a: Stabilized multi-tenant medical office in Los Angeles has generally traded between 5.5% and 6.75%, while single-tenant, investment-grade credit deals price tighter, often 5.0% to 5.75%. Actual pricing on any given building depends on remaining lease term, tenant credit, and seismic retrofit status, so treat these as a starting range rather than a fixed number.

faqs.q: Does an unpaid tenant improvement allowance count as boot?
faqs.a: An outstanding tenant improvement obligation is generally a liability consideration that affects net proceeds and debt-replacement math rather than boot itself, but the classification can vary by deal structure. Confirm the specific treatment with your tax advisor or qualified intermediary before it changes your identification math.

faqs.q: How does parking ratio affect which medical office buildings qualify as viable replacements?
faqs.a: Four to six stalls per 1,000 square feet is the practical floor for imaging centers and multi-specialty practices in Los Angeles, and buildings below that ratio typically struggle to retain or replace tenants at renewal. A low parking ratio should be priced into the underwriting rather than treated as a minor detail.

faqs.q: Can a vacant medical office building serve as replacement property?
faqs.a: Real property held for investment can generally qualify as like-kind replacement property regardless of current occupancy. Vacancy changes the underwriting and carry-cost picture, so review the specific facts with your qualified intermediary and tax advisor.

faqs.q: Why does underwriting take longer on multi-tenant medical office than single-tenant?
faqs.a: Multi-tenant buildings need a signed estoppel certificate from each physician-group tenant before closing, and small practice groups are typically slower to turn those documents around than a national credit tenant. Building extra time into the closing schedule for multi-tenant medical office protects the 180-day exchange period.
